newsitem.title: MEXICO: FORECAST-Alfa seen posting good results.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Alfa seen posting good results.

text.p: Mexican industrial firm Alfa SA is expected to show healthy 1996 profits as higher sales volumes in all its divisions offset weak prices in the company's petrochemical units.
An average of five industry analysts surveyed by Reuters forecast 1996 earnings per share of 6.86 pesos versus a 1995 earnings per share of about 3.71 per share, based on constant 1996 pesos.

Much of the yearly gain will be merely financial due to monetary gains. But some analysts also forecast a 10 percent real rise in peso earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization (EBITDA).

Company CEO Dionisio Garza Medina said on Wednesday the company's results would be "very good." He said weak revenues in the Petrotemex petrochemical unit and flat steel of its Hylsamex division were more than made up for by strong sales in the company's other areas.

Despite a stronger peso in real terms this year that could have hurt Alfa's exports, the company is diversified enough to have benefitted from a nascent recovery in the domestic economy, analysts said.
"Alfa has had a great year, despite a much stronger-than-expected peso," Kerry McHugh, an analyst at Goldman Sachs in New York, wrote in a recent report.

For the fourth quarter alone, McHugh said she expects a "slight improvement in EBITDA at Alfa from last quarter, mainly driven by a pickup at Hylsamex, which typically sees strong fourth-quarter shipments."
Analysts also said Alfa's Alpek unit has probably seen the worst of lower international petrochemical prices and will benefit going forward from a stronger domestic economy.
"Already, the company is noting a strong pick-up in its domestic sales, which generally offer higher margins than do exports," Abaco brokerage said in a recent report.
Alfa has divisions in petrochemicals (Alpek), steel (Hylsamex), food (Simga), telecommunications (Onexa) and retail (Versax). ((--David Luhnow, Mexico City newsroom, +525 728-9565))
